messages:
sara.oncall: heads up - customer MapleHealth escalated a p99 spike on hosted-prod at 09:12 UTC. They reported ~2.5x p99 token latency for generate endpoints. no immediate 500s, just very slow tails.

infra-bot: ALERT gpu-mem-high node=gpu-pool-12 mem_used=93% kv_cache=1.8GB p99_latency_ms=1420 baseline=620

alex.m: on it. can someone drop the grafana link for the range 08:45-09:30? want p50/p95/p99 and per-model breakdown. :eyes:

support-bot: https://grafana.internal/redwood/prod/p99?from=1700000000&to=1700003600 (MapleHealth routes: model-x-large, context=8k)

devin.ml: quick note - MapleHealth has a lot of long-prefix sessions from their legal-docs flow, KV growth expected. likely KV cache growth + fragmentation.

lisa.sre: confirmed. looked at node gpu-pool-12: multiple pods hitting 90%+ GPU memory but not OOMing. p99 jumps line up with sustained long-context sessions.

alex.m: can we capture a heap / GPU allocation map from one affected process? run something like:
```
kubectl exec -it pod/rt-model-x-7 -- bash
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
python -u -c "import psutil, json; print(json.dumps({'pid': psutil.Process().pid, 'rss': psutil.Process().memory_info().rss}))"
cat /proc/$(pgrep runtime)/maps | grep anon | wc -l
```

lisa.sre: paste from node (09:18):
```
PID, used_memory [MiB]
12345, 10340
12346, 10296
```
pmap shows dozens of small anonymous mappings. nvprof not available on prod, but vmmap suggests fragmentation.

devin.ml: that matches KV growth: KV cache per-request can balloon when clients upload long histories. if we don't cap per-session kv entries, we leak logical working set and allocator can't coalesce freed regions -> fragmentation.

sara.oncall: customer timeline: spike started after they rolled a client that includes a 6k-token system message. before that p99 ~620ms, after ~1.4s.

alex.m: quick mitigation options (short term):
- set per-route max_kv_tokens=1024 (config push) to limit KV growth
- temporarily reduce max_batch_size to keep per-GPU concurrency down (less peak memory)
- route heavy customers to a smaller model variant (model-x-medium) for warmfix
- graceful process restart on the most fragmented nodes to reclaim GPU memory (will cause short disruption)

lisa.sre: I prefer config changes first to avoid restarts. I can push a canary that enforces max_kv_tokens and lower batching on 2 pods in gpu-pool-12.

devin.ml: also add the logging to capture KV entry counts per request so we can quantify. minimal patch to runtime: log kv_entry_count in telemetry for generate calls. low overhead.

alex.m: i'll draft the hotfix patch for max_kv and kv telemetry. deploy plan: canary -> observe 15m -> scale canary -> roll if stable.

sara.oncall: repro steps (for QA/dev):
1) run loadtest against route /v1/generate with context 6k-8k, 1k tokens avg generation, concurrency 12
2) measure endpoint /internal/kv_size for pod every 30s
3) after 10m check p95/p99 and nvml memory usage
commands:
```
hey -c 12 -z 10m -t 60s -n 1000 POST https://api.redwood/prod/generate @long_context_payload.json
kubectl exec -it pod/rt-model-x-7 -- curl -s http://localhost:8080/internal/kv_size
watch -n 5 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv
```

lisa.sre: observed behaviour during test: kv_size climbs steadily then plateaus, but nvml free memory fragmented so allocations slow. 2 things: allocator fragmentation and no aggressive slab purging.

alex.m: allocator tuning options we can try (medium term):
- enable jemalloc background_thread and tunables to aggressive decay: MALLOC_CONF="dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000,background_thread:true"
- for tcmalloc, enable aggressive decommit flags if built with tcmalloc tunables
- reduce oversized buffer reuse thresholds in runtime so we reuse large buffers less often where they bloat fragmentation
- implement KV LRU eviction on insert when total_kv_bytes > threshold

devin.ml: adding LRU eviction is ideal long term. quick hack: cap per-request kv entries at ingestion time and evict oldest kv entries for a session.

lisa.sre: i've started a canary now: applied per-route max_kv_tokens=1024 and max_batch_size=6 to two pods (canary ids: rt-can-112, rt-can-113). will watch p99.

infra-bot: CANARY DEPLOY event: user=lisa.sre route=model-x-large pods=[rt-can-112,rt-can-113] config="max_kv_tokens=1024,max_batch_size=6"

sara.oncall: customer update queued: "We've identified a mitigation and are rolling it out. will update in 30m." :thumbsup:

alex.m: after canary (09:40) p99 for those pods dropped from 1.4s -> 720ms. overall node p99 improved ~20%. KV telemetry shows per-request kv entries capped ~900.

devin.ml: good signal. next steps:
- merge telemetry patch to main so we can correlate kv size with latency automatically
- plan allocator config rollout with SRE (jemalloc flags) next week during low traffic window
- schedule a controlled restart of the most fragmented nodes if fragmentation persists after config changes (coord with infra)

lisa.sre: putting action items in the incident doc. will keep MapleHealth in the loop.

sara.oncall: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with customer + postmortem draft after 24h observation. :rocket:

support-bot: MapleHealth notified: "Mitigation deployed to reduce KV growth and batching on impacted machines. We're monitoring and will follow up with details."

alex.m: FYI for postmortem: look at route-level defaults for max_kv_tokens across prod. may need safer defaults to prevent noisy neighbors causing tail latency.

sara.oncall: first_message_ts=2401234567 last_message_ts=2401234670 (thread closed for now, will reopen if regressions reappear)"
